# Which cars should join the museum tour?

**Add the 2021 Mercedes-AMG F1 W12 first, the SLS AMG Coupé Electric Drive second and the 1989 Sauber-Mercedes C 9 third.** Together they give visitors three new things to try: change an F1 wheel, steer a car with motor torque and put exhaust gas to work. The tour already has the 1950s W 196 R Formula 1 car. Its W 25 belongs to the pre-war Grand Prix era, and its 300 SLR is a sports racer. The gap is modern F1, alongside electric propulsion and Group C endurance racing. As of 26 November 2026, public sources establish gallery placement with different levels of confidence. The W12 has the strongest continuing visitor-facing exhibit record. [Current route](../stops/tour.js) · [Museum Pit Stop exhibit](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/formula-one-pit-stop/)

## Three cars to build around

| Priority and exhibit | What the visitor could do | Evidence for seeing it in Stuttgart |
|---|---|---|
| **1. 2021 Mercedes-AMG F1 W12 E Performance**, Legend 7 | Take one wheel change apart. Follow the wheel gun, centre nut, wheel and hub through removal and refitting, then try the physical rig. The W12 hangs vertically behind that rig. | The museum still lists the Pit Stop station. Its December 2024 announcement and photo identify the wall-mounted car as the W12. [Visitor exhibit](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/formula-one-pit-stop/) · [Museum identification and photo](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-02-PI-Boxenstopp-ENG.pdf) |
| **2. 2013 SLS AMG Coupé Electric Drive**, Legend 6 | Hold the steering angle steady through a bend and change the torque at the inside and outside wheels. With one motor per wheel, the difference in forward force helps rotate the car. The existing SLS stop shows the gullwing-door release on a different car. | Mercedes photographed a guide inside the electric SLS in Legend 6 in 2020. A March 2026 museum visit corroborates the electric car on display. [Museum photo](https://media.mercedes-benz.be/exclusive-insights-droomautos-uit-het-mercedes-benz-museum-op-instagram-tv/) · [2026 visit](https://www.theinteriorreview.com/story/2026/3/30/where-the-automobile-began-inside-the-mercedes-benz-museum-in-stuttgart-with-photos) · [Mercedes engineering description](https://media.mercedes-benz.nl/meest-exclusieve-en-dynamische-elektrische-sportwagen-ooit-mercedes-benz-sls-amg-coupe-electric-drive-de-krachtigste-supersportwagen-ter-wereld/) |
| **3. 1989 Sauber-Mercedes C 9, No. 63**, Legend 7 | Trace exhaust through one of the twin turbochargers. Turn the turbine and watch the compressor on the same shaft feed air back to the V8. Switch from roughly **530 kW in the race** to **up to 680 kW briefly in qualifying**. That gives the existing mechanically driven Roots blower a natural counterpart. | Mercedes names the actual Le Mans winner, its number and its gallery in 2019. Visitor footage dated November 2025 shows a C 9 on the banking. [Mercedes exhibit and race record](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/7c42293b-3c71-428d-af25-b562111e9844) · [Gallery footage at 6:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MShT3tfEHbk&t=363s) |

## Hamilton’s W11 would make the best second F1 stop

The **2020 W11** offers the best F1 mechanism to animate. Turn the steering wheel and the front wheels steer together. Push or pull it along its column and their **toe** changes: seen from above, their leading edges move closer together or farther apart. A top view with those two independent controls would explain what made dual-axis steering unusual. Mercedes explicitly placed Hamilton’s W11 in the **permanent Legend 7 exhibition in December 2024**. Confirm its current position before adding it to the walking route. [Museum statement](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-16-F1-Sonderpraesentation-ENG.pdf) · [FIA ruling describing the mechanism](https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/decision-document/2020%20Austrian%20Grand%20Prix%20-%20Decision%20-%20Protest%20-%20Car%2044.pdf)

**Mika Häkkinen’s 1998 McLaren-Mercedes MP4-13** would add the era when Mercedes supplied the engine and McLaren built the car. A November 2025 gallery film identifies it in Stuttgart. Its narrower track under the 1998 rules gives visitors a visible change to explore. It merits a fresh label photograph. Hamilton’s **2008 MP4-23**, by contrast, appeared in a six-car entrance-hall presentation with a published end date of **6 January 2025**. That show also featured the W05, W06, W08, W09 and W10. [MP4-13 gallery footage at 6:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MShT3tfEHbk&t=360s) · [Mercedes MP4-13 history](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/ddead055-42be-4bef-a636-f4be30241b02) · [Museum special presentation](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-16-F1-Sonderpraesentation-ENG.pdf)

**Leave Nico Rosberg’s 2016 W07 off the route for now.** Stuttgart tourism describes his title-winning car on the banking. Zaragoza’s Mobility City also identifies a W07 in its Stuttgart-sourced show, scheduled through **31 January 2027**. The sources do not resolve whether two examples are involved. The Spanish venue lists an original W25 too, making the existing tour’s W25 worth checking on the same visit. [Stuttgart tourism](https://presse.stuttgart-tourist.de/en/automobil-und-technik/die-geschichte-des-sterns-1) · [Zaragoza exhibit list](https://www.mobilitycity.es/n-oticias/mercedes-benz-lleva-a-mobility-city-en-zaragoza-su-legado-en-la-competicion-con-una-exposicion-inedita-en-espana/) · [Exhibition dates](https://www.mobilitycity.es/explora/actividades/mercedes-benz-motorsport-el-espiritu-de-las-flechas-de-plata-zaragoza/)

## Three further stops with mechanisms worth seeing

The **1994 NECAR 1** is the strongest follow-up for propulsion. Its fuel-cell installation filled the cargo compartment of an MB 100 van. Fade the body, increase the motor demand and follow hydrogen and air into the stack, electric current to the motor and water out. Mercedes identifies its archive photograph as taken in the Stuttgart museum, and a February 2025 visitor account photographs the van there. The numbered room still needs confirmation. [Mercedes archive and engineering account](https://media.mercedes-benz.pl/30-lat-temu-mercedes-benz-rozpocza-badania-nad-zastosowaniem-ogniw-paliwowych-w-motoryzacji/) · [2025 museum photographs](https://motorillustrated.com/mercedes-benz-museum-in-germany-4-electrified-models-not-to-be-missed/148994/)

The **1938 W 125 twelve-cylinder record car** adds a surprising cooling experiment. Ice and water around the radiator let engineers dispense with a conventional cooling-air intake for a short record run. A visitor could extend the run and watch the ice supply run out. Mercedes identifies the original in Legend 7 in 2018. For a record car with a dedicated museum listing today, the **1939 T 80** is another option. The permanent exhibit comprises the body, subframe and wheels. Its planned record run never took place, so the W 125 supplies the better story about measured performance. [W 125 gallery placement](https://media.mercedes-benz.it/mercedes-benz-w-125-inesauribile-fonte-dispirazione/) · [Mercedes history of both cars](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/f9a48175-8964-490e-9909-9f35cbea8a6f) · [T 80 museum exhibit](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/t-80-record-giant-from-1939/)

The **1960 Mercedes-Benz 300 measuring car** could enrich a stop already in the tour. In 2022 the museum described the one-off wagon in Legend 5 with a cable linking it to the 220 S ahead. In road tests that cable carried measurements back to engineers and their recording equipment. An interaction could send the lead car over a bump, follow an illustrative sensor signal along the cable and replay the trace. A fresh photo of the pair would also resolve the tour’s open question about the 220 S’s gallery. [Museum account of the paired display](https://mb-france.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/2022/02/2022Messwagentxt.pdf)

## From shortlist to walking route

The most valuable visit would start at the Legend 7 Pit Stop and banking. A photograph of each car with its adjacent label would settle the W11 and McLaren questions and establish where a visitor should stand. In Legend 6, a photograph of the electric SLS would give the new stop its own reference image. If a dated temporary stop fits the tour, the museum also schedules the **eSprinter and eActros 600 in Collection 5 through 4 April 2027**. That end date belongs on any visitor-facing entry. [Museum exhibition announcement](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/f1be3681-993f-4ac9-bc02-e2b8878ddcc4)

# Give visitors a reason to look twice

**Visitor review · 26 November 2026 · local revision `d868721`**

At the 300 SL, a visitor can look up at the gullwing door, lower the sides of its virtual frame, and see the structure lose roughly two-thirds of its stiffness in the model. That is the tour at its best. The room picker and three-stop highlights now make that experience easier to reach. **The first priority is trustworthy wayfinding** — two published exhibit locations conflict with the route, and the link back from a stop loses the visitor’s gallery. The strongest content addition would be one verified Legend 6 exhibit that explains emission-free propulsion. For visual impact, some of the best material is already built and waiting to be discovered. [300 SL experiment](../stops/300sl/car.js) · [Walking route](../stops/tour.js)

## Visitors can find their room and still lose their place

In an iPhone-sized WebKit viewport, “Find your room” brought the room picker and first gallery into the same screen. Legend 6 opened correctly in English and Hungarian, and the highlights entry opened three named stories. On the SLK, the pinned stage stayed visible while the roof opened, and its four phases fit in both languages. On the Gullwing, the selected frame survived a language change. These are tangible improvements over the earlier walkthrough. [Mobile walkthrough](<../research_notes/Museum tour visitor review/ux.md>) · [Earlier visitor review](../docs/visitor-experience-proposal.md)

| Where | What happens | Change and retest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Returning from the SLK | “Tour route” goes to the index introduction. A visitor who came from a shared stop link must find Legend 6 again. | Point the standard header at the existing room fragment. From a fresh SLK link, reach the neighboring Legend 6 cards in one tap. Preserve the highlights return journey. [Stop navigation](../lib/app/shell.js) |
| Choosing Collection 4 | The picker gives a level without the uncertainty qualifier that appears at the gallery heading. | Put the same qualifier beside the level where visitors choose it. Check both locations after floor verification. [Room picker](../lib/app/index.js) |
| Returning to the SLK photo | Shared background copy calls the image a “museum photo” even though this stop identifies it as a reference image. | Use “Back at the car” or “photo” in the shared transition. Check one museum photograph and one reference photograph in each supported language. [Story copy](../lib/app/story.js) · [SLK](../stops/slk/car.js) |

## Eleven galleries cover the building unevenly

**46 stops cover all seven Legend rooms and Collections 1–4.** Legend 1 alone has eight stops. Legend 6 has four, covering suspension and combustion, a folding roof, crash structure, and escape hinges. A visitor could complete that gallery and miss its account of the transition to emission-free mobility entirely. Pick one object confirmed on display and let visitors trace energy from its source to the wheels. If that vehicle supports regeneration, reverse the trace under braking. Collection 5’s changing exhibitions and the Level 0 technology area also merit short, dated directions at the appropriate point in the walk. [Tour inventory](../stops/tour.js) · [Museum exhibition guide, pp. 3–4](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/content/dam/brandhub/assets/art-and-culture/mercedes-benz-museum/museum/Media-Information-Mercedes-Benz-Museum-EN.pdf) · [Museum’s Legend 6 description](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/legend-6/)

**Verify two locations before directing another visitor there with confidence.** The tour places the Blitzen-Benz, one of its three highlights, in Legend 2. Stuttgart’s tourism office puts it on the banked racing curve, which the museum identifies with Legend 7. The O 302 appears under Collection 1 with an uncertainty marker. Daimler Truck’s November 2022 photographs place the World Cup bus in Collection 4. Those photos also show two excellent identification cues, the fan by the front door and the Tip and Tap mascots at the rear. Obtain a dated floor or curator check, carry the result through the picker, route order, stop header and highlights, then try finding each vehicle from its gallery entrance. Until then, show visitors which placement was last documented and when. [Stuttgart tourism office](https://presse.stuttgart-tourist.de/en/automobil-und-technik/die-geschichte-des-sterns-1) · [Museum exhibition guide](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/content/dam/brandhub/assets/art-and-culture/mercedes-benz-museum/museum/Media-Information-Mercedes-Benz-Museum-EN.pdf) · [Daimler Truck’s O 302 photo captions](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/maximum-bus-comfort-for-the-1974-world-cup-footballers-52102483)

## One good question unlocks an existing model

The route has **64 component entries using 24 subsystem types**. Nineteen entries have a dedicated prompt, 17 have an answer, and 18 include a real-part illustration. Other entries teach through controls and prose, so these figures measure editorial structure. The LP 333 shows where a small edit could pay off. Its twin-steer model already displays individual wheel angles, slip and turning radius. Ask visitors to hold the first axle at 20°, predict which tyres will scrub, then fix the second axle straight. The reveal is the second pair sliding sideways because they point away from their rolling paths around the turn. A visitor who can point to those tyres and explain the scrub has understood more than a slip-angle readout alone conveys. [Inventory method](<../research_notes/Museum tour visitor review/engineering.md>) · [LP 333](../stops/lp333/car.js) · [Twin-steer controls](../subsystems/twin-steer.js)

Two answers need tighter bounds. The 300 SLR’s lift graph and moving rocker show exactly when the spring valve loses contact. Saying the second cam closes its valve “at any speed” extends the claim beyond the displayed experiment. Write “The second cam pulls the valve shut throughout the speed range shown.” The Evo II wing answer gives about 34 kg extra rear-axle load and 9 kW extra drag power at 200 km/h. Grid refinement affects the magnitude. Lead with what held up across runs — rear load and drag power both increased — and place the figures beside that qualification. Retest by asking visitors which result they would expect on the real car and which numbers came from this simulation. [300 SLR valve story](../stops/300slr/car.js) · [Evo II experiments](../stops/190e-evo2/car.js)

## The most memorable details reward a closer look

**Best visual reveal:** the Evo II wheel-arch tracer. Follow air headed for the tyre and watch it turn outward past the door. The final stop contains this striking demonstration, far from the route entrance and outside the three highlights. Feature a direct invitation, “Follow the air around a racing tyre,” that lands on the experiment. Test whether a first-time visitor can follow the same stream before and after it passes the wheel. A quieter technical Easter egg is the Gullwing crankshaft’s 30° step control. Walking through the rotation lets visitors discover the mirrored piston pairs and see their shaking forces cancel. [Evo II tracer](../stops/190e-evo2/car.js) · [Gullwing engine balance](../stops/300sl/car.js)

**Best opportunity for visual polish:** the 300 SLR closing rocker. The visitor can already swap the animation with an enlarged photograph of a real Ducati rocker, identified as the donor. The photo has an accessible button name and a desktop zoom cursor, but the touch caption begins “In real life” and the visible swap instruction appears on the return journey. Add a visible “Enlarge part photo” cue. Mark the closing fork in the same colour and position where feasible in both views, with a stationary marker for reduced motion. Hand someone the phone and ask them to find what pulls the valve shut. See whether they enlarge the picture unaided and can point to the fork in each view. [Photo interaction](../lib/app/story.js) · [300 SLR part and caption](../stops/300slr/car.js)

## What to validate on the next museum visit

Begin in a gallery with a shared stop link. Can someone identify the exhibit from its photograph, reach the adjacent cars, and find one feature on the physical vehicle that the model helped them understand? Run that short task at the disputed Blitzen-Benz location, the LP 333 and the 300 SLR. It tests navigation, historical placement and learning in the setting where all three matter together.

This review combined a routed-content inventory and published museum material with local WebKit walks in reduced motion on emulated iPhone and landscape iPad profiles. The English and Hungarian checks sampled particular journeys. # Give visitors a reason to look twice

**Visitor review · 26 November 2026 · local revision `d868721`**

At the 300 SL, a visitor can look up at the gullwing door, lower the sides of its virtual frame, and see the structure lose roughly two-thirds of its stiffness in the model. That is the tour at its best. The room picker and three-stop highlights now make that experience easier to reach. **The first priority is trustworthy wayfinding** — two published exhibit locations conflict with the route, and the link back from a stop loses the visitor’s gallery. The strongest content addition would be one verified Legend 6 exhibit that explains emission-free propulsion. For visual impact, some of the best material is already built and waiting to be discovered. [300 SL experiment](../stops/300sl/car.js) · [Walking route](../stops/tour.js)

## Visitors can find their room and still lose their place

In an iPhone-sized WebKit viewport, “Find your room” brought the room picker and first gallery into the same screen. Legend 6 opened correctly in English and Hungarian, and the highlights entry opened three named stories. On the SLK, the pinned stage stayed visible while the roof opened, and its four phases fit in both languages. On the Gullwing, the selected frame survived a language change. These are tangible improvements over the earlier walkthrough. [Mobile walkthrough](<../research_notes/Museum tour visitor review/ux.md>) · [Earlier visitor review](../docs/visitor-experience-proposal.md)

| Where | What happens | Change and retest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Returning from the SLK | “Tour route” goes to the index introduction. A visitor who came from a shared stop link must find Legend 6 again. | Point the standard header at the existing room fragment. From a fresh SLK link, reach the neighboring Legend 6 cards in one tap. Preserve the highlights return journey. [Stop navigation](../lib/app/shell.js) |
| Choosing Collection 4 | The picker gives a level without the uncertainty qualifier that appears at the gallery heading. | Put the same qualifier beside the level where visitors choose it. Check both locations after floor verification. [Room picker](../lib/app/index.js) |
| Returning to the SLK photo | Shared background copy calls the image a “museum photo” even though this stop identifies it as a reference image. | Use “Back at the car” or “photo” in the shared transition. Check one museum photograph and one reference photograph in each supported language. [Story copy](../lib/app/story.js) · [SLK](../stops/slk/car.js) |

## Eleven galleries cover the building unevenly

**46 stops cover all seven Legend rooms and Collections 1–4.** Legend 1 alone has eight stops. Legend 6 has four, covering suspension and combustion, a folding roof, crash structure, and escape hinges. A visitor could complete that gallery and miss its account of the transition to emission-free mobility entirely. Pick one object confirmed on display and let visitors trace energy from its source to the wheels. If that vehicle supports regeneration, reverse the trace under braking. Collection 5’s changing exhibitions and the Level 0 technology area also merit short, dated directions at the appropriate point in the walk. [Tour inventory](../stops/tour.js) · [Museum exhibition guide, pp. 3–4](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/content/dam/brandhub/assets/art-and-culture/mercedes-benz-museum/museum/Media-Information-Mercedes-Benz-Museum-EN.pdf) · [Museum’s Legend 6 description](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/legend-6/)

**Verify two locations before directing another visitor there with confidence.** The tour places the Blitzen-Benz, one of its three highlights, in Legend 2. Stuttgart’s tourism office puts it on the banked racing curve, which the museum identifies with Legend 7. The O 302 appears under Collection 1 with an uncertainty marker. Daimler Truck’s November 2022 photographs place the World Cup bus in Collection 4. Those photos also show two excellent identification cues, the fan by the front door and the Tip and Tap mascots at the rear. Obtain a dated floor or curator check, carry the result through the picker, route order, stop header and highlights, then try finding each vehicle from its gallery entrance. Until then, show visitors which placement was last documented and when. [Stuttgart tourism office](https://presse.stuttgart-tourist.de/en/automobil-und-technik/die-geschichte-des-sterns-1) · [Museum exhibition guide](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/content/dam/brandhub/assets/art-and-culture/mercedes-benz-museum/museum/Media-Information-Mercedes-Benz-Museum-EN.pdf) · [Daimler Truck’s O 302 photo captions](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/maximum-bus-comfort-for-the-1974-world-cup-footballers-52102483)

## One good question unlocks an existing model

The route has **64 component entries using 24 subsystem types**. Nineteen entries have a dedicated prompt, 17 have an answer, and 18 include a real-part illustration. Other entries teach through controls and prose, so these figures measure editorial structure. The LP 333 shows where a small edit could pay off. Its twin-steer model already displays individual wheel angles, slip and turning radius. Ask visitors to hold the first axle at 20°, predict which tyres will scrub, then fix the second axle straight. The reveal is the second pair sliding sideways because they point away from their rolling paths around the turn. A visitor who can point to those tyres and explain the scrub has understood more than a slip-angle readout alone conveys. [Inventory method](<../research_notes/Museum tour visitor review/engineering.md>) · [LP 333](../stops/lp333/car.js) · [Twin-steer controls](../subsystems/twin-steer.js)

Two answers need tighter bounds. The 300 SLR’s lift graph and moving rocker show exactly when the spring valve loses contact. Saying the second cam closes its valve “at any speed” extends the claim beyond the displayed experiment. Write “The second cam pulls the valve shut throughout the speed range shown.” The Evo II wing answer gives about 34 kg extra rear-axle load and 9 kW extra drag power at 200 km/h. Grid refinement affects the magnitude. Lead with what held up across runs — rear load and drag power both increased — and place the figures beside that qualification. Retest by asking visitors which result they would expect on the real car and which numbers came from this simulation. [300 SLR valve story](../stops/300slr/car.js) · [Evo II experiments](../stops/190e-evo2/car.js)

## The most memorable details reward a closer look

**Best visual reveal:** the Evo II wheel-arch tracer. Follow air headed for the tyre and watch it turn outward past the door. The final stop contains this striking demonstration, far from the route entrance and outside the three highlights. Feature a direct invitation, “Follow the air around a racing tyre,” that lands on the experiment. Test whether a first-time visitor can follow the same stream before and after it passes the wheel. A quieter technical Easter egg is the Gullwing crankshaft’s 30° step control. Walking through the rotation lets visitors discover the mirrored piston pairs and see their shaking forces cancel. [Evo II tracer](../stops/190e-evo2/car.js) · [Gullwing engine balance](../stops/300sl/car.js)

**Best opportunity for visual polish:** the 300 SLR closing rocker. The visitor can already swap the animation with an enlarged photograph of a real Ducati rocker, identified as the donor. The photo has an accessible button name and a desktop zoom cursor, but the touch caption begins “In real life” and the visible swap instruction appears on the return journey. Add a visible “Enlarge part photo” cue. Mark the closing fork in the same colour and position where feasible in both views, with a stationary marker for reduced motion. Hand someone the phone and ask them to find what pulls the valve shut. See whether they enlarge the picture unaided and can point to the fork in each view. [Photo interaction](../lib/app/story.js) · [300 SLR part and caption](../stops/300slr/car.js)

## What to validate on the next museum visit

Begin in a gallery with a shared stop link. Can someone identify the exhibit from its photograph, reach the adjacent cars, and find one feature on the physical vehicle that the model helped them understand? Run that short task at the disputed Blitzen-Benz location, the LP 333 and the 300 SLR. It tests navigation, historical placement and learning in the setting where all three matter together.

# Museum coverage

## Which galleries does the route represent?

### Takeaway

There are 46 stops across 11 named galleries. All seven Legend galleries and Collections 1–4 have stops. Collection 5 hosts changing exhibitions, and the official tour includes a Level 0 technology area beyond the racing finale. [Route](../../stops/tour.js) · [Museum exhibition description, pp. 3–4](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/content/dam/brandhub/assets/art-and-culture/mercedes-benz-museum/museum/Media-Information-Mercedes-Benz-Museum-EN.pdf)

### Cited Findings

- Legend 1–7 stop counts are 8, 3, 4, 4, 6, 4, 4. Collection 1–4 counts are 3, 4, 2, 4. The museum explicitly places the Uhlenhaut Coupé in Legend 4, matching a strong tour stop. [Route](../../stops/tour.js) · [Museum guide](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/content/dam/brandhub/assets/art-and-culture/mercedes-benz-museum/museum/Media-Information-Mercedes-Benz-Museum-EN.pdf)
- The four Legend 6 entries teach suspension and combustion, a folding roof, a crash structure and escape hinges. The room itself tells the transition to emission-free mobility. [Route](../../stops/tour.js) · [Official Legend 6](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/legend-6/)

### Inferences

- Choose one verified electrification exhibit for Legend 6. Let the visitor follow energy through the powertrain at launch and under braking if that exhibit supports regeneration. Add a dated Collection 5 signpost and an optional Level 0 exit prompt. These cover more of the physical visit without promising a permanent rotating exhibit.

### Gaps

- No current object-by-object inventory or floor inspection. These counts measure guide coverage only.

## Which locations warrant checking first?

### Takeaway

Two published descriptions conflict with walking directions, including one of the three teaser stops.

### Cited Findings

- The route places Blitzen-Benz in Legend 2 without a warning. Stuttgart’s tourism office places it on the banked racing curve, which the museum identifies as Legend 7. [Route](../../stops/tour.js) · [Stuttgart tourism press office](https://presse.stuttgart-tourist.de/en/automobil-und-technik/die-geschichte-des-sterns-1) · [Museum guide](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/content/dam/brandhub/assets/art-and-culture/mercedes-benz-museum/museum/Media-Information-Mercedes-Benz-Museum-EN.pdf)
- The O 302 stop already flags room uncertainty but sorts into Collection 1. Dated November 2022 photos explicitly place this World Cup recreation in Collection 4. The manufacturer’s photographs show the fan by the front door and the Tip and Tap mascots on the rear, two useful physical recognition cues. [Route](../../stops/tour.js) · [Daimler Truck photo captions](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/maximum-bus-comfort-for-the-1974-world-cup-footballers-52102483)

### Inferences

- Prioritize a dated floor or curator check for these two stops. Publish the last documented gallery and date alongside any unresolved current location. Check route index, stop header and teaser order after correction.

### Gaps

- A dated press photo establishes past placement. Current floor placement and exhibit loans remain unverified.

# Mobile visitor experience

## Can I enter the right room?

### Takeaway

The November 18 proposal’s two biggest navigation requests have shipped. A return journey from a stop still loses the selected room.

### Cited findings

- In local WebKit with iPhone 15 emulation (393 × 659 CSS pixels), “Find your room” put the bottom of the room picker at y=366 and the first gallery at y=398. Tapping Legend 6 reached the correct heading in English and Hungarian. The route rendered 46 cards. The highlights opened three named stories. [Index](../../index.html) · [Route rendering](../../lib/app/index.js)
- On a normal stop, the header’s “Tour route” goes to ./, even after entering from Legend 6. A visitor looking for a different car in the same room lands back at the introduction. Browser Back is a workaround for direct arrivals from the route. Link the normal header to the existing room fragment. Keep the highlights return path. [Header](../../stop.html) · [Routing](../../lib/app/shell.js)
- In the picker, Collection 4 looks as certain as every other floor assignment. The room heading only qualifies the level after the visitor jumps. Use the existing level qualification at the decision point until the placement is verified. [Picker and heading](../../lib/app/index.js)

### Inferences

- Validate by starting from a shared SLK stop link and reaching its neighboring gallery cards in one tap.

### Gaps

- Emulation does not establish wayfinding success in Stuttgart.

## Can I operate the exhibit while reading?

### Takeaway

The roof gives visitors a concrete action, visible progression and a way to keep the illustration in view.

### Cited findings

- Opening the SLK roof changed the live state to “Opening” in English and “Nyílik” in Hungarian. The pinned stage was 223 px tall on the phone. Four phases fitted without document overflow in both languages. Hungarian also fitted on a landscape iPad Pro 11 profile (1194 × 834). [Roof controls](../../subsystems/vario-roof.js) · [Story](../../lib/app/story.js)
- The Gullwing’s lower-sill selection survived an English/Hungarian switch in both directions. The corresponding experiment remained selected after reload. This check sampled the immediate post-switch readout before animation had settled, so it does not establish the final stiffness value. [State restoration](../../lib/app/story.js)
- The stage now mounts the identifying photo before loading Three.js. Remaining copy issue: the background step describes the returning image as the “museum photo” for every car, including the explicitly identified SLK reference image. Use “Back at the car” or a neutral “photo” in this shared sentence. [Stage](../../lib/app/viewer.js) · [Shared background copy](../../lib/app/story.js) · [SLK data](../../stops/slk/car.js)

### Inferences

- This fixes specific issues from the prior review. Do not repeat “add room jump”, “show the photo first” or “add three highlights” as new work. [Earlier review](../../docs/visitor-experience-proposal.md)

### Gaps

- Reduced motion was enabled for these scripted walks. There was no physical-device, airplane-mode, VoiceOver or German interaction test in this pass.

## Can I discover the closer look?

### Takeaway

Some part pictures double as a full-size comparison. Its affordance is weakest on touch screens.

### Cited findings

- The real-part photo is a button with a descriptive accessible name and a desktop zoom cursor. Its visible figure caption starts “In real life”. A tap swaps the image and live model. Scrolling the figure away restores the normal arrangement. The existing visible swap instruction is for swapping back. [Story interaction](../../lib/app/story.js) · [Styles](../../lib/app/theme.css)

### Inferences

- Add a small visible “Enlarge part photo” affordance on eligible pictures. In a first-use test, ask someone to inspect the real part closely without first teaching the gesture.

### Gaps

- This discoverability judgment comes from implementation inspection. No observed participant missed the control in this review.
# Engineering, explanation and visual discovery

## Where does the visitor get to reason like an engineer?

### Takeaway

Across the 46 routed stops, 64 component entries use 24 subsystem types. Nineteen entries declare a prompt, 17 an answer and 18 a real-part illustration. These counts measure use of the story template. Some other entries guide the visitor through panel labels or explanatory paragraphs. Counts were obtained by importing every routed English car module at d868721. [Route](../../stops/tour.js) · [Story rendering](../../lib/app/story.js)

### Cited findings

- The 300 SL asks why its doors hinge at the roof. Switching to a low-sided frame reduces calculated stiffness to roughly a third in this model. It turns a feature visitors can see across the room into a structural experiment. [300 SL](../../stops/300sl/car.js)
- The LP 333 already lets visitors steer or fix the second front axle and watch its tyres scrub. Its readouts include turning radius, separate wheel angles and degrees of slip. Its component omits the dedicated prompt and answer fields. [Truck](../../stops/lp333/car.js) · [Controls](../../subsystems/twin-steer.js)

### Inferences

- First copy pass: open the LP 333 experiment with “Hold the first axle at 20°. What happens to the second pair of tyres when you fix them straight?” Follow the experiment with a sentence linking the sideways drag to the wheels' turning centre. Success means a visitor can point to the affected wheels and explain why they scrub.

### Gaps

- A template count cannot establish comprehension. Validate with a first-time visitor before extending prompts across all 64 entries.

## Which claims could visitors misread?

### Takeaway

The tour distinguishes illustrative geometry and calculated results in detailed notes. A visitor who reads only the answer can still leave with more certainty than the model supports.

### Cited findings

- The Evo II wing answer gives about 34 kg of extra rear-axle load at 200 km/h and 9 kW extra drag power. It names the whole-car model, but only later explains that grid refinement changes the size of the effect. The nose and arch experiments already limit their claims to visible flow where stronger comparisons are unavailable. [Evo II wing, nose and arch](../../stops/190e-evo2/car.js)
- The 300 SLR invites visitors to raise rpm until a spring valve floats. A moving cursor ties the lift graph to the mechanism. The answer qualifies the spring threshold as illustrative but says the desmo valve follows at “any speed”; that follows from the model imposing the cam motion on that valve. [Car text](../../stops/300slr/car.js) · [Simulation display](../../subsystems/desmo-valvetrain.js)

### Inferences

- Give the Evo wing's repeatable direction of change first. Put load and power beside the coarse-grid caveat under wind-tunnel details. For the SLR, “The second cam pulls the valve shut throughout the speed range shown” preserves the discovery and bounds the claim.

### Gaps

- This was a source-level review of the teaching sequence. It does not establish the accuracy of historic race-car settings.

## Where is the wow already built?

### Takeaway

Let visitors discover one detail they could tell another person beside the car. Three existing interactions already do that.

### Cited findings

- The 300 SL balance experiment lets visitors step 30° through crank rotation and see how mirrored piston pairs cancel shaking forces. The Evo II wheel-arch tracer follows air starting in line with the tyre as it deflects out past the door. The SLR pairs an animated closing rocker with a tappable real Ducati rocker photo and clearly identifies the donor mechanism. [300 SL balance](../../stops/300sl/car.js) · [Evolution II trace](../../stops/190e-evo2/car.js) · [SLR rocker](../../stops/300slr/car.js) · [Photo swap](../../lib/app/story.js)
- The ready-made three-stop teaser omits the Evo II, the final stop in the full route. [Route and teaser](../../stops/tour.js)

### Inferences

- A low-cost featured link to “Follow the air around a racing tyre” could bring that last-stop reveal to the route entrance. Keep the teaser's three-stop promise intact. For visual polish, use the existing camera/colour pairing to briefly pick out the closing fork in the SLR photo and model when the visitor swaps views. Provide a stationary marker for reduced motion. The check is whether someone can point to the part that closes the valve in both views.

### Gaps

- The proposed highlights and featured link are design ideas. Their effect on task completion needs a visitor test.

The museum’s 2 December 2024 release identifies the 2021 W12 mounted vertically behind the station, separate from the apparatus visitors use to change wheels. The Mercedes archive photograph of the arrangement is D845673. [Museum station](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/formula-one-pit-stop/) · [Museum release and caption](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-02-PI-Boxenstopp-ENG.pdf)
- The museum explicitly identified Hamilton’s 2020 W11 in its permanent Legend 7 display on 16 December 2024. [Museum announcement](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-16-F1-Sonderpraesentation-ENG.pdf)

### Inferences

- Design W12 around changing a wheel: pause an exploded hub, wheel and central nut at each stage and compare with the physical pit-stop rig. In April 2026, Zaragoza’s Mobility City specifically identified a W07 Hybrid and an original W25 in its Stuttgart-sourced exhibition, scheduled 27 March 2026–31 January 2027. The organizer described tours of that exhibition on 23 November 2026. The 1939 three-axle T 80 is a secondary choice if the tour wants a spectacular unfinished engineering project. - The record attempt never ran. The museum exhibit includes the body, grid subframe and wheels. The original chassis was prepared separately with a cutaway DB 603 engine. [Mercedes-Benz](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/f9a48175-8964-490e-9909-9f35cbea8a6f)

### Inferences

- Use the silhouette and the planned powerplant to model how required power rises with speed, explicitly marking all top speeds as targets or estimates. This overlaps with existing aero stops, so rank the C 9 and W 125 record car first. [Museum](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/t-80-record-giant-from-1939/)

### Gaps

- No measured performance from a record run exists. No current same-day availability feed identified. [Mercedes-Benz](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/f9a48175-8964-490e-9909-9f35cbea8a6f)
# Passenger and experimental cars

## Which road car adds the most to the route?

### Takeaway

Choose the Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG Coupé Electric Drive. The current SLS story shows a 2010 car photographed outdoors and models its gullwing-door release. A separately identified electric variant would give Legend 6 a working electric drivetrain. [Current SLS stop](../../stops/sls/car.js) · [Museum guide in the exhibit](https://media.mercedes-benz.be/exclusive-insights-droomautos-uit-het-mercedes-benz-museum-op-instagram-tv/)

### Cited Findings

- Mercedes photographed museum guide Pádraic Ó Leanacháin in the electric SLS in Legend 6 in 2020. A March 2026 illustrated visit also identifies the 2013 SLS AMG Electric Drive on the museum floor. [Museum guide in Legend 6](https://media.mercedes-benz.be/exclusive-insights-droomautos-uit-het-mercedes-benz-museum-op-instagram-tv/) · [March 2026 visit](https://www.theinteriorreview.com/story/2026/3/30/where-the-automobile-began-inside-the-mercedes-benz-museum-in-stuttgart-with-photos)
- Four electric motors drive the wheels individually, permitting active distribution of both drive and braking torque. The manufacturer describes the systems and production launch in 2013. [Mercedes-Benz technical release](https://media.mercedes-benz.nl/meest-exclusieve-en-dynamische-elektrische-sportwagen-ooit-mercedes-benz-sls-amg-coupe-electric-drive-de-krachtigste-supersportwagen-ter-wereld/)

### Inferences

- Put the car in a constant-radius turn and let the visitor vary the torque split between the inside and outside wheels. Mark force at each tyre and show how the imbalance helps turn the car. Photograph the electric exhibit itself. Its four-motor layout is a distinct story from either the existing SLS hinge release or the tour’s mechanical differential locks.

### Gaps

- These are dated sightings and gallery assignments. They cannot guarantee that a particular vehicle is present every day in November 2026.

## Which research vehicle adds an entirely different power source?

### Takeaway

The 1994 NECAR 1 prototype makes hydrogen fuel-cell propulsion visible at vehicle scale. Mercedes documented the actual MB 100-based van inside its Stuttgart museum and a visitor photographed it there in a report published in February 2025. [Mercedes-Benz archive photo and vehicle history](https://media.mercedes-benz.pl/30-lat-temu-mercedes-benz-rozpocza-badania-nad-zastosowaniem-ogniw-paliwowych-w-motoryzacji/) · [On-site photos](https://motorillustrated.com/mercedes-benz-museum-in-germany-4-electrified-models-not-to-be-missed/148994/)

### Cited Findings

- The experimental power unit filled the van’s entire load compartment. The official release explicitly identifies its photograph as taken in the Mercedes-Benz Museum in Stuttgart. [Mercedes-Benz archive photograph D312958](https://media.mercedes-benz.pl/30-lat-temu-mercedes-benz-rozpocza-badania-nad-zastosowaniem-ogniw-paliwowych-w-motoryzacji/)
- The same 2025 photographer saw the 2010 B-Class fuel-cell car and NECAR 1. Use the photographs for floor evidence, and manufacturer sources for engineering detail. [February 2025 visit](https://motorillustrated.com/mercedes-benz-museum-in-germany-4-electrified-models-not-to-be-missed/148994/)

### Inferences

- Let the visitor increase motor demand and trace hydrogen and air into the stack, current to the traction motor and water out. Fade the van body to show what happened to its cargo space. Use the B-Class as an optional visual comparison of packaging, without promising a second adjacent exhibit.

### Gaps

- The accessible manufacturer source confirms the Stuttgart museum, without identifying the numbered room. Verify exact floor placement before publishing wayfinding.

## Which vehicle would make a distinctive engineering stop alongside one already present?

### Takeaway

The 1960 Mercedes-Benz 300 measuring car (Messwagen) is a one-off development laboratory. Its cable literally connects it to the subject of the existing 220 S stop. [Museum Close-Up, February 2022](https://mb-france.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/2022/02/2022Messwagentxt.pdf)

### Cited Findings

- The museum describes the 300 and the W 111 220 S connected by the cable in Legend 5. Real test engineers followed the development vehicle, keeping the bulky instruments in the following car, and generally recorded the incoming data on magnetic tape. [Mercedes-Benz Museum exhibit account](https://mb-france.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/2022/02/2022Messwagentxt.pdf)
- The route has a separate 300 and 220 S, without a Messwagen entry. [Tour route](../../stops/tour.js)

### Inferences

- A visitor could drive the front car over a bump, trace the signal through the cable, then replay the trace on the recorder in the following car. The official source explains the instrumentation principle. The illustrated sensor channel should be described as an example unless the chosen measurement is documented for the exhibit. The paired display also helps clarify the existing 220 S stop’s room.

### Gaps

- The museum’s detailed description is from 2022. It proves the exact paired gallery display on that date, without certifying today’s installation. For a tightly evidenced first phase the electric SLS is stronger. The eSprinter and eActros 600 are separate temporary alternatives in Collection 5, officially scheduled 28 June 2026–4 April 2027. [Special exhibition announcement](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/f1be3681-993f-4ac9-bc02-e2b8878ddcc4)

id: "desmo", label: "Desmodromic valves", subsystem: "desmo-valvetrain",
      prompt: "Raise the engine speed. Where does the spring-closed valve stop following the cam?",
      answer: "Above about 7,000 rpm in this model, at the top of the lift: there the valve has to slow down and turn back faster than its spring can make it, so it flies on, off the cam. The desmodromic valve is pulled shut by a second cam and follows the cam at any speed.",
      view: { pos: [0.02, -0.4, 0.52], target: [-0.4, 0.02, 0.37] },
      ghost: { fill: 0, edge: 0 },
      params: {
        label: "Desmodromic valve vs a spring-closed valve",
        cam: { lift: 0.01, open: 0.6, duration: 2.27, mass: 0.1, preload: 0.008, floatRpm: 7000, base: 0.018 },
        rpm: { min: 2000, max: 9500, value: 5000 },
        origin: [-0.4, 0, 0.35],
      },
      real: {   // the part in real life (not this car)
        src: "parts/desmo-ducati.jpg", w: 800, h: 600,
        alt: "Close-up through the inspection opening of a Ducati motorcycle engine: an upper rocker on the valve tip and a forked rocker under the collar on the stem",
        caption: "On this Ducati engine, the forked rocker pulls the valve shut by the collar on its stem; the upper rocker opens it. Which rocker pulls the valve shut in the Mercedes model? The rocker layouts differ; the idea, closing by force, is the same.",
        credit: { author: "Gérard Delafond", license: "CC BY-SA 3.0", url: "https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Desmo_photo.jpg" },
      },
      talk: [
        "At high revs a valve spring can no longer pull the valve back fast enough: the valve floats off the cam and can hit the piston. Raise the speed and watch the spring valve's line leave the dashed cam line.",
        "Mercedes's desmodromic gear has no closing spring. A second cam and a rocker pull the valve shut, so the valve follows the cam exactly at any speed.",
        "The opening and closing cams are matched: their radii always add up to the same value, so the two never fight. Ducati later made the idea famous on motorcycles.",
      ],
    },
      id: "wing", label: "Rear wing", subsystem: "race-aero",
      prompt: "Watch the orange arrow in the dashed box above the wing's trailing edge. Raise the flap: which way does the air leaving the wing turn?",
      answer: "Upward. With the flap raised, the mean direction of the air in the box tips about 13° further up (about 8° on a coarser grid). Turning the air upward takes a push, and the wing feels the push back, downward. In the whole-car model that is about 34 kg more on the rear axle at 200 km/h, for about 9 kW more of the engine's power spent on drag.",
      more: "Wind tunnel details",
      view: { pos: [-3.73, 1.88, 1.12], target: [-3.73, 0.238, 1.12] },
      ghost: { fill: 0, edge: 0 },
      params: {
        label: "Wing flap · a slice of the whole-car tunnel",
        data: "stops/190e-evo2/cfd/wing/", start: "base",
        // Crop of the whole-car runs (tools/cfd/part.mjs wing; results in tools/cfd/results/wing.json); flap size illustrative.
        cases: [
          { id: "base", label: "Baseline", say: "Flap down: note the orange arrow, the mean direction of the air leaving the trailing edge in the dashed box." },
          { id: "flap", label: "Flap raised", say: "Flap raised: in the same box the air tips upward, about 13° more than with the flap down, and the paths behind the wing bend up with it." },
        ],
      },
      talk: [
        "The racing car's rear wing carries an upper flap that teams could raise for circuits with fast bends. Mercedes-Benz names a retractable upper flap and a two-position front spoiler for the homologation car; the flap here is an illustrative size and angle, not the 1992 setting.",
        "The picture is a slice 238 mm from the car's centre line, cut out of a 3-D wind tunnel of the whole car. Colour shows how fast the air moves up (red) or down (blue), as a share of the road speed; grey is solid: the boot lid, the wing and, when raised, the flap.",
        "The orange arrow is the mean direction of the air in the dashed box, over 48 of the model's 28 mm cells. Raising the flap tips it up by about 13°; on a coarser 40 mm grid, with 12 cells in the box, by about 8°. Both grids agree that it tips upward. The angles before and after depend on where the box sits, so only the change is given.",
        "In the whole-car model, raising the flap adds about 34 kg of load on the rear axle at 200 km/h (25 to 43 kg on its two grids) and about 9 kW of drag power (4 to 14 kW); the front axle hardly changes. More rear load is grip and stability in fast bends; the drag is speed lost on the straights.",
        "The model is a game mesh of the Evo II filled with 28 mm blocks: half the car with a mirror on the centre line, a moving road, wheels held still, and a Reynolds number about 300 times smaller than the real car's. Read the change between the two settings, not the values.",
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "wheel-arch", label: "Front wheel arch", subsystem: "race-aero",
      prompt: "Seen from above at hub height: the bumper corner, the front tyre in its flared arch, the door behind. Tap Follow the air: the blue line is a path of the mean flow, the average route of the air, from in front of the car.",
      answer: "It starts 78 cm from the car's centre line, in line with the tyre, and the car's front corner turns it outward. It never comes back in: by the dashed line, 60 cm behind the axle, it runs about 37 cm further out, well clear of the door. Along the flank behind the arch the air moves slower (green and blue) than in the fast stream outside (red).",
      more: "Wind tunnel details",
      view: { pos: [0, 1.3, 3.8], target: [0, 0.75, 0.344] },
      ghost: { fill: 0, edge: 0 },
      params: {
        label: "Front corner · seen from above at hub height",
        data: "stops/190e-evo2/cfd/wheel-arch/", start: "fitted", follow: true,
        // Local 3-D run of the front corner (tools/cfd/part.mjs evo-arch, tools/cfd/corner.mjs).
        cases: [{ id: "fitted", label: "Flared arch", say: "This path of the mean flow starts in line with the tyre, just in front of the bumper corner. The car's front corner turns it about 37 cm outward, and it keeps that line past the door." }],
      },
      talk: [
        "The Evolution II's arches were widened so that wider wheels and tyres would fit under the body, and shaped with the rest of the body kit in the wind tunnel.",
        "The picture is a level slice at hub height through a 3-D wind tunnel of the front corner, computed ahead of time from the same game mesh as the rear wing. Colour is the air's speed against the road speed; grey is solid, body and tyre cut through. The blue line follows the time-averaged flow in this level slice; a single puff of air wanders around it with the turbulence.",
        "The tyre stands still in its carved-out wheelhouse, 48 mm above a moving road; the body is cut flat 1 m up and the half car is mirrored at the centre line. It was computed on one grid of 24 mm cells: over five flow-throughs the outward shift stays between 36.7 and 37.7 cm. A finer grid was not run, so the figure is rounded.",
        "There is no second arch here to compare with. The mesh's flare already sits within a centimetre of the tyre's outer face, so a narrower arch could not cover the tyre: the lesson is where the air goes. Nothing here separates what the flare does from what the bumper corner and the tyre do.",
      ],
    },

  "Limited-slip: friction plates between the left side gear and the carrier resist the two sides turning apart. Das Rad mit Haftung kann ein Mehrfaches des Drehmoments am rutschenden Rad aufnehmen, hier das {0}-Fache, ohne dass die Achse je starr wird."],
  "Open: the spider gears share the torque equally between the side gears. The slipping wheel can take only a little, so its partner gets just as little, and the spider gears let the slipping wheel spin.": ["Nyitott: a kiegyenlítő kerekek egyenlően osztják el a nyomatékot a féltengely-kerekek között. A kipörgő kerék csak keveset tud átvinni, így a párja is csak ugyanannyit kap, a kiegyenlítő kerekek pedig hagyják, hogy a kipörgő kerék pörögjön.", "Offen: Die Ausgleichskegelräder teilen das Drehmoment gleich auf die Achswellenräder auf. Das rutschende Rad kann nur wenig übertragen, also bekommt sein Partner genauso wenig, und die Ausgleichskegelräder lassen das rutschende Rad durchdrehen."]
 }}
EOF

The search turned up consistent specs for the SLS AMG Coupé Electric Drive, mostly from the 2012 launch coverage.

- **Power and torque:** The car uses four electric motors producing a total output of 552 kW and maximum torque of 1000 Nm. The motors are synchronous and sit one per corner, which gives permanent all-wheel drive.
- **Torque dynamics:** The drivetrain has two separate gearboxes that provide direct drive to each axle, along with a new AMG Torque Dynamics system that distributes drive to individual wheels based on traction.
- **Battery:** Coverage gives a energy content of 60 kWh and battery voltage of 400 volts. The pack weighs 548 kg and is made of 12 modules, each holding 72 lithium-ion cells.
- **Performance:** The car reaches 100 km/h in just 3.9 seconds. Its top speed is 250 km/h*, and the asterisk marks it as electronically limited.
- **Charging and price:** Home charging uses a 22 kW quick-charge function. The launch price was 416,500 euros (incl. 19% VAT) in Germany.

I did not find the original Mercedes-AMG press release itself; these figures come from secondary sites that reproduce it. The sources also disagree on the rating: one gives a 600 kW electric load potential for the battery, and the press-release text says Range 250 km (according to NEDC).

The search turned up consistent turbo details but conflicting boost figures, with the C9's power varying by boost setting and season.

**Turbos:** Wikipedia lists the C9's engine as a 4,973 cc 90° V8 with Twin KKK Type 27 Turbos. Another source describes the engine as the 5.0-litre engine remained largely unchanged from its road-going counterpart but came equipped with two off-the-shelf KKK turbochargers.

**Boost and power:**
- Wikipedia says that after the 1989 addition of 16-valve heads, power rose by about 20 hp to around 720 hp at 1.6 bar and 7,000 RPM.
- The same article says that absolute power could also be taken from just under 800 hp with 2.2 bar of boost to about 820 hp.
- Race limits are reported as maximum race boost was 1.9 bar. That conflicts with the 2.2 bar figure above, which likely reflects qualifying or non-race settings. One source notes there were no special qualifying engines and on 2.2 bar of boost it was said to be rated at "almost 800 hp".
- A Grokipedia entry claims boost pressure was effectively capped at around 2.5 bar absolute. This is an AI-generated wiki and doesn't match the other sources, so treat it with caution.

**Engine variant:** The M119 HL was developed by Mercedes-Benz AG for Group C World Championship Race events based on the production engine used for the Mercedes-Benz passenger car range. The SAE paper gives the latest version a power output of 530 kW.

**Related context:** The successor C11 was reported to go up to 2.4 Bar and make 850 hp at 7,000 RPM in high boost.

Overall, the sources agree on KKK twin turbos and about 720 hp at roughly 1.6 bar. They disagree on the peak boost. Race-limit (1.9 bar) and qualifying/high-boost (2.2 bar+) figures are the most reliable differences to note. For exact specifications, the SAE paper and Mercedes-Benz archival material would be the best primary references, and I didn't find those in this search.

# Give visitors a reason to look twice

**Visitor review · 26 November 2026 · local revision `d868721`**

At the 300 SL, a visitor can look up at the gullwing door, lower the sides of its virtual frame, and see the structure lose roughly two-thirds of its stiffness in the model. That is the tour at its best. The room picker and three-stop highlights now make that experience easier to reach. **The first priority is trustworthy wayfinding** — two published exhibit locations conflict with the route, and the link back from a stop loses the visitor’s gallery. The strongest content addition would be one verified Legend 6 exhibit that explains emission-free propulsion. For visual impact, some of the best material is already built and waiting to be discovered. [300 SL experiment](../stops/300sl/car.js) · [Walking route](../stops/tour.js)

## Visitors can find their room and still lose their place

In an iPhone-sized WebKit viewport, “Find your room” brought the room picker and first gallery into the same screen. Legend 6 opened correctly in English and Hungarian, and the highlights entry opened three named stories. On the SLK, the pinned stage stayed visible while the roof opened, and its four phases fit in both languages. On the Gullwing, the selected frame survived a language change. These are tangible improvements over the earlier walkthrough. [Mobile walkthrough](<../research_notes/Museum tour visitor review/ux.md>) · [Earlier visitor review](../docs/visitor-experience-proposal.md)

| Where | What happens | Change and retest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Returning from the SLK | “Tour route” goes to the index introduction. A visitor who came from a shared stop link must find Legend 6 again. | Point the standard header at the existing room fragment. From a fresh SLK link, reach the neighboring Legend 6 cards in one tap. Preserve the highlights return journey. [Stop navigation](../lib/app/shell.js) |
| Choosing Collection 4 | The picker gives a level without the uncertainty qualifier that appears at the gallery heading. | Put the same qualifier beside the level where visitors choose it. Check both locations after floor verification. [Room picker](../lib/app/index.js) |
| Returning to the SLK photo | Shared background copy calls the image a “museum photo” even though this stop identifies it as a reference image. | Use “Back at the car” or “photo” in the shared transition. Check one museum photograph and one reference photograph in each supported language. [Story copy](../lib/app/story.js) · [SLK](../stops/slk/car.js) |

## Eleven galleries cover the building unevenly

**46 stops cover all seven Legend rooms and Collections 1–4.** Legend 1 alone has eight stops. Legend 6 has four, covering suspension and combustion, a folding roof, crash structure, and escape hinges. A visitor could complete that gallery and miss its account of the transition to emission-free mobility entirely. Pick one object confirmed on display and let visitors trace energy from its source to the wheels. If that vehicle supports regeneration, reverse the trace under braking. Collection 5’s changing exhibitions and the Level 0 technology area also merit short, dated directions at the appropriate point in the walk. [Tour inventory](../stops/tour.js) · [Museum exhibition guide, pp. 3–4](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/content/dam/brandhub/assets/art-and-culture/mercedes-benz-museum/museum/Media-Information-Mercedes-Benz-Museum-EN.pdf) · [Museum’s Legend 6 description](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/legend-6/)

**Verify two locations before directing another visitor there with confidence.** The tour places the Blitzen-Benz, one of its three highlights, in Legend 2. Stuttgart’s tourism office puts it on the banked racing curve, which the museum identifies with Legend 7. The O 302 appears under Collection 1 with an uncertainty marker. Daimler Truck’s November 2022 photographs place the World Cup bus in Collection 4. Those photos also show two excellent identification cues, the fan by the front door and the Tip and Tap mascots at the rear. Obtain a dated floor or curator check, carry the result through the picker, route order, stop header and highlights, then try finding each vehicle from its gallery entrance. Until then, show visitors which placement was last documented and when. [Stuttgart tourism office](https://presse.stuttgart-tourist.de/en/automobil-und-technik/die-geschichte-des-sterns-1) · [Museum exhibition guide](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/content/dam/brandhub/assets/art-and-culture/mercedes-benz-museum/museum/Media-Information-Mercedes-Benz-Museum-EN.pdf) · [Daimler Truck’s O 302 photo captions](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/maximum-bus-comfort-for-the-1974-world-cup-footballers-52102483)

## One good question unlocks an existing model

The route has **64 component entries using 24 subsystem types**. Nineteen entries have a dedicated prompt, 17 have an answer, and 18 include a real-part illustration. Other entries teach through controls and prose, so these figures measure editorial structure. The LP 333 shows where a small edit could pay off. Its twin-steer model already displays individual wheel angles, slip and turning radius. Ask visitors to hold the first axle at 20°, predict which tyres will scrub, then fix the second axle straight. The reveal is the second pair sliding sideways because they point away from their rolling paths around the turn. A visitor who can point to those tyres and explain the scrub has understood more than a slip-angle readout alone conveys. [Inventory method](<../research_notes/Museum tour visitor review/engineering.md>) · [LP 333](../stops/lp333/car.js) · [Twin-steer controls](../subsystems/twin-steer.js)

Two answers need tighter bounds. The 300 SLR’s lift graph and moving rocker show exactly when the spring valve loses contact. Saying the second cam closes its valve “at any speed” extends the claim beyond the displayed experiment. Write “The second cam pulls the valve shut throughout the speed range shown.” The Evo II wing answer gives about 34 kg extra rear-axle load and 9 kW extra drag power at 200 km/h. Grid refinement affects the magnitude. Lead with what held up across runs — rear load and drag power both increased — and place the figures beside that qualification. Retest by asking visitors which result they would expect on the real car and which numbers came from this simulation. [300 SLR valve story](../stops/300slr/car.js) · [Evo II experiments](../stops/190e-evo2/car.js)

## The most memorable details reward a closer look

**Best visual reveal:** the Evo II wheel-arch tracer. Follow air headed for the tyre and watch it turn outward past the door. The final stop contains this striking demonstration, far from the route entrance and outside the three highlights. Feature a direct invitation, “Follow the air around a racing tyre,” that lands on the experiment. Test whether a first-time visitor can follow the same stream before and after it passes the wheel. A quieter technical Easter egg is the Gullwing crankshaft’s 30° step control. Walking through the rotation lets visitors discover the mirrored piston pairs and see their shaking forces cancel. [Evo II tracer](../stops/190e-evo2/car.js) · [Gullwing engine balance](../stops/300sl/car.js)

**Best opportunity for visual polish:** the 300 SLR closing rocker. The visitor can already swap the animation with an enlarged photograph of a real Ducati rocker, identified as the donor. The photo has an accessible button name and a desktop zoom cursor, but the touch caption begins “In real life” and the visible swap instruction appears on the return journey. Add a visible “Enlarge part photo” cue. Mark the closing fork in the same colour and position where feasible in both views, with a stationary marker for reduced motion. Hand someone the phone and ask them to find what pulls the valve shut. See whether they enlarge the picture unaided and can point to the fork in each view. [Photo interaction](../lib/app/story.js) · [300 SLR part and caption](../stops/300slr/car.js)

## What to validate on the next museum visit

Begin in a gallery with a shared stop link. Can someone identify the exhibit from its photograph, reach the adjacent cars, and find one feature on the physical vehicle that the model helped them understand? Run that short task at the disputed Blitzen-Benz location, the LP 333 and the 300 SLR. It tests navigation, historical placement and learning in the setting where all three matter together.

This review combined a routed-content inventory and published museum material with local WebKit walks in reduced motion on emulated iPhone and landscape iPad profiles. The English and Hungarian checks sampled particular journeys. Current floor placement, physical-device behavior, German interaction, VoiceOver, offline use and first-time visitor comprehension remain for a separate field or device check. [Walkthrough details](<../research_notes/Museum tour visitor review/ux.md>) · [Coverage evidence](<../research_notes/Museum tour visitor review/coverage.md>)

// Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé (W 196 S), 1955. Frame: mm, x forward, y left, z up; origin = front axle centre at
// wheel-centre height. Bore, stroke, displacement and wheelbase from the sources; firing order, lean, rods and valve-train
// numbers are illustrative.
export default {
  slug: "300slr",
  title: "Inside the Uhlenhaut Coupé",
  name: "Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé",
  year: 1955,
  summary: "A Grand Prix-derived straight-eight with direct petrol injection, and valves closed by cams instead of springs.",
  eyebrow: "Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé (W 196 S), 1955",
  question: "How do you close a valve without a spring?",
  lede: "The racing sports car that Rudolf Uhlenhaut drove on the road. Two mechanisms: the straight-eight with fuel sprayed straight into the cylinders, and the desmodromic valve gear that let it rev where springs give up.",
  frame: { origin: "front", wheelbase: 2370, wheelR: 330 },
  orbit: { min: 0.3, max: 12 },
  sun: [3, 4, 6],
  body: {
    ghost: [
      { pts: [[400, -120], [400, 430], [-1000, 520], [-3200, 540], [-3500, 380], [-3520, -120]], y: [-850, 850] },   // body, traced from the photo
      { pts: [[900, -120], [900, 150], [700, 330], [400, 430], [400, -120]], y: [-560, 560] },                       // nose
      { pts: [[-1000, 520], [-1300, 790], [-1800, 820], [-2500, 760], [-3200, 540]], y: [-560, 560] },               // cabin
      { torus: { R: 290, r: 40, pos: [0, 665, 0], rot: [90, 0, 0] }, mirror: true },
      { torus: { R: 290, r: 40, pos: [-2370, 690, 0], rot: [90, 0, 0] }, mirror: true },
    ],
  },
  photo: {
    src: "photo.jpg", w: 1200, h: 803,
    alt: "Silver 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé on display in the Mercedes-Benz Museum, seen from the front right",
    cam: { c: [2793.9, -2105.5, 1189.9], yaw: 2.5851, pitch: -0.2559, roll: -0.0614, f: 1291 }, // tools/photo-fits/300slr.json
    credit: { author: "Valder137", license: "CC BY 2.0", url: "https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:REDACTED%C3%A8_RSideFront_MBMuse_9June2013_(14960622596).jpg" },
  },
  components: [
    {
      id: "engine", label: "Straight-eight", subsystem: "inline-engine",
      view: { pos: [1.0, 1.35, 0.85], target: [-0.55, 0, 0.15] },
      ghost: { fill: 0.03, edge: 0.45 },
      params: {
        label: "Four-stroke cycle · eight cylinders, direct injection",
        order: [1, 6, 2, 5, 8, 3, 7, 4],            // generic straight-eight order: the M196's own is not confirmed
        bore: 78, stroke: 78, rod: 140,             // rod length illustrative
        xs: [-250, -340, -430, -520, -610, -700, -790, -880],
        crankZ: 0, lean: 33,                        // engine laid over to one side; angle per CMC, unverified
        valvetrain: "dohc", ignition: "spark", fuel: "direct",
        speed: { min: 5, max: 60, value: 20 },
      },
      talk: [
        "This is the straight-eight of the W 196 Grand Prix car, enlarged for sports-car racing: 78 mm bore and stroke, 2,982 cc and about 310 PS.",
        "A Bosch pump sprays fuel straight into each cylinder during the intake stroke, watch for the spray. Daimler-Benz knew direct injection from its aero engines.",
        "The engine is laid over to one side so the bonnet can sit low. Uhlenhaut, head of the test department, used this coupé as his company car; it could reach about 290 km/h.",
        "Only two coupés were built. In 2022 Mercedes-Benz sold the other one for 135 million euros, the highest price ever paid for a car.",
      ],
    },
    {

# Which cars should join the museum tour?

**Add the 2021 Mercedes-AMG F1 W12 first, the SLS AMG Coupé Electric Drive second and the 1989 Sauber-Mercedes C 9 third.** Together they give visitors three new things to try: change an F1 wheel, steer a car with motor torque and put exhaust gas to work. The tour already has the 1950s W 196 R Formula 1 car. Its W 25 belongs to the pre-war Grand Prix era, and its 300 SLR is a sports racer. The gap is modern F1, alongside electric propulsion and Group C endurance racing. As of 26 November 2026, public sources establish gallery placement with different levels of confidence. The W12 has the strongest continuing visitor-facing exhibit record. [Current route](../stops/tour.js) · [Museum Pit Stop exhibit](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/formula-one-pit-stop/)

## Three cars to build around

| Priority and exhibit | What the visitor could do | Evidence for seeing it in Stuttgart |
|---|---|---|
| **1. 2021 Mercedes-AMG F1 W12 E Performance**, Legend 7 | Take one wheel change apart. Follow the wheel gun, centre nut, wheel and hub through removal and refitting, then try the physical rig. The W12 hangs vertically behind that rig. | The museum still lists the Pit Stop station. Its December 2024 announcement and photo identify the wall-mounted car as the W12. [Visitor exhibit](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/formula-one-pit-stop/) · [Museum identification and photo](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-02-PI-Boxenstopp-ENG.pdf) |
| **2. 2013 SLS AMG Coupé Electric Drive**, Legend 6 | Hold the steering angle steady through a bend and change the torque at the inside and outside wheels. With one motor per wheel, the difference in forward force helps rotate the car. The existing SLS stop shows the gullwing-door release on a different car. | Mercedes photographed a guide inside the electric SLS in Legend 6 in 2020. A March 2026 museum visit corroborates the electric car on display. [Museum photo](https://media.mercedes-benz.be/exclusive-insights-droomautos-uit-het-mercedes-benz-museum-op-instagram-tv/) · [2026 visit](https://www.theinteriorreview.com/story/2026/3/30/where-the-automobile-began-inside-the-mercedes-benz-museum-in-stuttgart-with-photos) · [Mercedes engineering description](https://media.mercedes-benz.nl/meest-exclusieve-en-dynamische-elektrische-sportwagen-ooit-mercedes-benz-sls-amg-coupe-electric-drive-d
| **3. 1989 Sauber-Mercedes C 9, No. 63**, Legend 7 | Trace exhaust through one of the twin turbochargers. Turn the turbine and watch the compressor on the same shaft feed air back to the V8. Switch from roughly **530 kW in the race** to **up to 680 kW briefly in qualifying**. That gives the existing mechanically driven Roots blower a natural counterpart. | Mercedes names the actual Le Mans winner, its number and its gallery in 2019. Visitor footage dated November 2025 shows a C 9 on the banking. [Mercedes exhibit and race record](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/7c42293b-3c71-428d-af25-b562111e9844) · [Gallery footage at 6:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MShT3tfEHbk&t=363s) |

## Hamilton’s W11 would make the best second F1 stop

The **2020 W11** offers the best F1 mechanism to animate. Turn the steering wheel and the front wheels steer together. Push or pull it along its column and their **toe** changes: seen from above, their leading edges move closer together or farther apart. A top view with those two independent controls would explain what made dual-axis steering unusual. Mercedes explicitly placed Hamilton’s W11 in the **permanent Legend 7 exhibition in December 2024**. Confirm its current position before adding it to the walking route. [Museum statement](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-16-F1-Sonderpraesentation-ENG.pdf) · [FIA ruling describing the mechanism](https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/decision-document/2020%20Austrian%20Grand%20Prix%20-%20Decision%20-%20Protest%20-%20Car%2044.pdf)

**Mika Häkkinen’s 1998 McLaren-Mercedes MP4-13** would add the era when Mercedes supplied the engine and McLaren built the car. A November 2025 gallery film identifies it in Stuttgart. Its narrower track under the 1998 rules gives visitors a visible change to explore. It merits a fresh label photograph. Hamilton’s **2008 MP4-23**, by contrast, appeared in a six-car entrance-hall presentation with a published end date of **6 January 2025**. That show also featured the W05, W06, W08, W09 and W10. [MP4-13 gallery footage at 6:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MShT3tfEHbk&t=360s) · [Mercedes MP4-13 history](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/ddead055-42be-4bef-a636-f4be30241b02) · [Museum special presentation](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-16-F1-Sonderpraesentation-ENG.pdf)

**Leave Nico Rosberg’s 2016 W07 off the route for now.** Stuttgart tourism describes his title-winning car on the banking. Zaragoza’s Mobility City also identifies a W07 in its Stuttgart-sourced show, scheduled through **31 January 2027**. The sources do not resolve whether two examples are involved. The Spanish venue lists an original W25 too, making the existing tour’s W25 worth checking on the same visit. [Stuttgart tourism](https://presse.stuttgart-tourist.de/en/automobil-und-technik/die-geschichte-des-sterns-1) · [Zaragoza exhibit list](https://www.mobilitycity.es/n-oticias/mercedes-benz-lleva-a-mobility-city-en-zaragoza-su-legado-en-la-competicion-con-una-exposicion-inedita-en-espana/) · [Exhibition dates](https://www.mobilitycity.es/explora/actividades/mercedes-benz-motorsport-el-espiritu-de-las-flechas-de-plata-zaragoza/)

## Three further stops with mechanisms worth seeing

The **1994 NECAR 1** is the strongest follow-up for propulsion. Its fuel-cell installation filled the cargo compartment of an MB 100 van. Fade the body, increase the motor demand and follow hydrogen and air into the stack, electric current to the motor and water out. Mercedes identifies its archive photograph as taken in the Stuttgart museum, and a February 2025 visitor account photographs the van there. The numbered room still needs confirmation. [Mercedes archive and engineering account](https://media.mercedes-benz.pl/30-lat-temu-mercedes-benz-rozpocza-badania-nad-zastosowaniem-ogniw-paliwowych-w-motoryzacji/) · [2025 museum photographs](https://motorillustrated.com/mercedes-benz-museum-in-germany-4-electrified-models-not-to-be-missed/148994/)

The **1938 W 125 twelve-cylinder record car** adds a surprising cooling experiment. Ice and water around the radiator let engineers dispense with a conventional cooling-air intake for a short record run. A visitor could extend the run and watch the ice supply run out. Mercedes identifies the original in Legend 7 in 2018. For a record car with a dedicated museum listing today, the **1939 T 80** is another option. The permanent exhibit comprises the body, subframe and wheels. Its planned record run never took place, so the W 125 supplies the better story about measured performance. [W 125 gallery placement](https://media.mercedes-benz.it/mercedes-benz-w-125-inesauribile-fonte-dispirazione/) · [Mercedes history of both cars](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/f9a48175-8964-490e-9909-9f35cbea8a6f) · [T 80 museum exhibit](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibit

The **1960 Mercedes-Benz 300 measuring car** could enrich a stop already in the tour. In 2022 the museum described the one-off wagon in Legend 5 with a cable linking it to the 220 S ahead. In road tests that cable carried measurements back to engineers and their recording equipment. An interaction could send the lead car over a bump, follow an illustrative sensor signal along the cable and replay the trace. A fresh photo of the pair would also resolve the tour’s open question about the 220 S’s gallery. [Museum account of the paired display](https://mb-france.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/2022/02/2022Messwagentxt.pdf)

## From shortlist to walking route

The most valuable visit would start at the Legend 7 Pit Stop and banking. A photograph of each car with its adjacent label would settle the W11 and McLaren questions and establish where a visitor should stand. In Legend 6, a photograph of the electric SLS would give the new stop its own reference image. If a dated temporary stop fits the tour, the museum also schedules the **eSprinter and eActros 600 in Collection 5 through 4 April 2027**. That end date belongs on any visitor-facing entry. [Museum exhibition announcement](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/f1be3681-993f-4ac9-bc02-e2b8878ddcc4)

The most valuable visit would start at the Legend 7 Pit Stop and banking. In Legend 6, a photograph of the electric SLS would give the new stop its own reference image. lines: +// A Formula 1 wheel change at one corner, as a timeline (docs/TOUR-POC.md §6). Pure: no DOM, no three.js.
+// Phases run one after another: the car stops on its marks, the jacks lift it, the gun undoes the centre nut, the old wheel
+// comes off the hub, the new one goes on, the gun tightens the nut, the jacks drop. Each phase { id, dur (s) }.
+// stuck: the gun meets the nut at an angle, cuts its drive lugs and can no longer turn it (Monaco 2021): the stop never ends.
+export const PHASES = [
+  { id: "stop", dur: 0.25 }, { id: "lift", dur: 0.2 }, { id: "undo", dur: 0.3 }, { id: "off", dur: 0.35 },
+  { id: "on", dur: 0.35 }, { id: "tighten", dur: 0.3 }, { id: "drop", dur: 0.25 },
+export const total = (phases = PHASES) => phases.reduce((s, p) => s + p.dur, 0);
+const smooth = u => u * u * (3 - 2 * u);
